sam: Heads up — long-context perf run (32k tokens) showing steady GPU memory growth on MI250 only. H100 runs clean. Reproducer attached, OOM after ~12 minutes. Trace suggests paged-KV eviction completes but freeable pages never reclaimed, reuse window keeps growing.

maria: saw a similar trend in nightly. Noticed lots of small fragments in the page map and increasing slab counts. Possible that evict completion path is dropping a stale owner flag on MI driver.

joshuar: Can you share the repro command + trace link? I want to check kernel selection differences (tiling vs linear) — MI kernels pick different tilers which might change coalescing behavior.

sam: repro is: 
```
python tools/repro_longctx.py --model tiny-llama --seq 32768 --batch 1 --kv-page-size 65536 --prefetch False --device mi250
```
Trace bundle: s3://redwood-perf/4332109876/longctx_trace.zip (perf, gpu timelines, and runtime logs).

bench-bot: perf artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/4332109876/longctx_trace.zip :white_check_mark:

maria: Quick log excerpt: 
```
[2026-02-12T14:22:11Z] kv_evict: candidate_count=128 evicted=128 completed=128 reclaimable=0
[2026-02-12T14:22:11Z] pt_unmap: stale_owner_detected=17
[2026-02-12T14:22:12Z] kv_alloc: slab_fragments=194 free_pages=0
```
Feels like evict path reports evicted but PT still holds references.

dmitri: On MI we have different PCI page migration timing and the GPU driver returns pagefree asynchronously. Hypothesis: our evict completion callback runs before driver-level unmap, so slab accounting thinks pages are freed but page table still maps them -> reuse sees them as live and increments fragment count. Could be exacerbated by sparse-tiling kernel paths (those do more fine-grained writes).

sam: Good catch. I toggled `KV_EVICT_SYNC=1` locally (force host sync on evict) and the leak didn't reproduce for a short run — memory plateaued. Not a fix but points to ordering.

joshuar: Also looked at kernel selection logs: H100 picks tiled_coalesce_v2, MI picks tiled_coalesce_legacy. Legacy path doesn't run the post-coalesce compact step that merges adjacent page refs. That could explain fragment growth.

maria: If we add a conservative fallback that forces compact after eviction on MI devices, should stabilize until we fix driver ordering. Patch idea: after evict completion, call `pt_compact_range(start, end)` before marking pages reclaimable.

dmitri: Agreed. Another mitigation: increase `kv_page_size` to 128k for MI to reduce fragment surface area and tweak batcher to favor shorter request window so reuse window doesn't stretch. Both are tunable from runtime config.

sam: I'll open a small PR with a guarded compact (MI-only, opt-in env KV_PT_COMPACT=1) and a benchmark job. If it passes, we'll roll to nightly and see longctx stability.

joshuar: For the PR, include a micro-benchmark comparing tiled_coalesce_{v2,legacy} with synthetic traffic and attach nvprof/rocm-trace outputs. Also add a unit-test that fakes delayed driver unmap and asserts reclaimable count goes to zero.

maria: One more note — check batching heuristics: our current dynamic-batcher allows large in-flight prefixes for longctx which increases the number of active KV segments; lowering max_batch_tokens reduced memory pressure in a quick test. Might be a low-risk config change to ship sooner.

sam: Thanks — action items: 1) sam: PR with MI-only compact, bench job (today). 2) joshuar: attach tiled kernel traces and microbench (tomorrow). 3) maria: run nightly with kv_page_size=128k + lower max_batch_tokens and report. 4) dmitri: follow up on driver ticket with vendor about async unmap ordering.

maria: tagging @dmitri and @joshuar for visibility. :mag:

bench-bot: CI job queued: kv-evict-compact-mi (run id 4332110440)

sam: I'll paste the PR link when ready. Thanks all.
